q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT EMAIL FROM (SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AS A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL FROM (SELECT EMAIL, COUNT(*) FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AS A
counterexample: INSERT INTO PERSON (ID, EMAIL) VALUES (1, 'user1@example.com'), (2, 'user2@example.com'), (3, NULL);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses the GROUP BY clause directly on the EMAIL column, which can lead to unexpected results if the EMAIL column contains NULL values. Q2, on the other hand, first groups by EMAIL and then selects from the subquery, which avoids the issue with NULL values.
